Since the beginning of my trial, I have used 9 credits and 40GB of storage... about $19.60 worth of resources. Snowflake costs could balloon pretty fast... I'd recommend setting up resource monitors, and only use XSMALL warehouses; credits consumed doubles each size up.

Vertica about 10x cheaper than Snowflake, per a Vertica-funded benchmark comparing Eon Mode to Snowflake.

The monthly bill does make me wince, but Snowflake includes all server and compute costs, no installation or upgrades... It's genuine SaaS, very simple to manage and optimise so less DBA or DevOps manpower needed. Expensive, but lower TCO than alternatives I suspect.
The problem with Snowflake is particularly worse due to its lack of query level attribution of costs and no in-built features for monitoring or recommendations on improvements.

You would think they would be saving (and charging the customer!) a bundle not enforcing constraints on their tables... to the customer it's simply unforgivable to have cosmetic constraints on a database.

The issue with dbt models in Snowflake is that if you perform a full-refresh and don't sort it, you ruin any natural clustering from an incremental model. Auto-clustering gets too expensive at scale and Snowflake doesn't give much guidance on alternatives.

Snowflake has continuously improved performance resulting in reduced credit consumption... The CFO forecasted a $97 million shortfall guiding for 2022 revenue resulting from product improvements; stock dropped immediately after.
I predict we'll see more people choosing Clickhouse over Snowflake in the next 5 years... and give people a better escape hatch if they want to self-host their data stack.
[Disclaimer: former Snowflake employee] Snowflake is not expensive because of perverse incentives... It is expensive because it is a highly differentiated and very sticky product.
